items.title: Ready for the future?
items.description: A RECENT McKinsey report outlines three forces reshaping organisations globally — technology and artificial intelligence (AI), economic and geopolitical disruption, and a changing workforce. These forces may appear less immediate to Pakistani business leaders, who already contend with volatile costs, uncertain demand, disrupted supply chains and regulatory uncertainty, amongst other existential issues. With these new challenges, naturally, the question arises: how prepared are our organisations for change? It is a crucial question, but I believe a more fundamental one lies beneath; are Pakistani organisations ready to learn? This shift in focus stems from my belief that organisations should prioritise building capability over simply adopting the latest technology or management ideas. Capability encompasses an organisation’s accumulated ability to achieve its purpose; making sound decisions, developing people, learning from experience and adapting to changing circumstances. Results are undoubtedly important — profit, growth, market share, impact and productivity — but they alone do not define good management. The more important question is whether an organisation is becoming more capable of fulfilling its purpose. Are they making better decisions? Are their people developing? Does experience influence behaviour? Can they respond to environmental changes? And would they continue to perform even if their most senior leader were no longer present? With new challenges, a fundamental question arises: are Pakistani organisations prepared to learn? These questions hold particular relevance for Pakistan. We boast many highly capable founders, family-business leaders and senior executives whose market knowledge, relationships and judge­­­ment have often propelled successful enterprises throu­­gh challenging times. However, personal capability alone does not equate to institutional capability. I have witnessed organisations where every significant decision ultimately falls to the owner(s) or the most experienced person. This applies to difficult customers, major investments, hiring decisions and operational problems — everyone waits for the person who is assumed to know the answer. While this can work well in the short term, with a capable individual at the centre, it leads to a growing dependence on that single person. Managers become adept at escalating problems rather than solving them, and experience becomes concentrated in a few heads rather than embedded in systems, processes and shared judgement. The organisation might grow larger or become more profitable, but it has not necessarily become stronger. True leadership is not measured by whether everything functions when the leader is present; it is whether the organisation has become more capable in their absence. This is one reason Pakistani organisations often struggle with succession. We tend to think of succession as simply finding the next CEO or family member, but it is a much broader question. Has the organisation developed people capable of making decisions? Has it created systems that do not rely on personal intervention? Has it made knowledge accessible beyond those who acquired it? Has it given capable younger managers real exposure to challenging work before they are expected to lead? If not, the organisation may have found a successor, but it has not built succession. The same issue arises with AI. Many leaders are asking which tasks AI can automate, which is a reasonable starting point. However, the more important question is what new capabilities the organisation will need when routine work changes. Technology matters. AI will change how work is done, which skills matter and what customers expect. But technology does not transform an organisation. People using technology differently might. A company can buy the latest systems, appoint a chief digital officer and run pilots in AI. It can still make the same slow decisions, hide the same bad news, reward the same behaviour and depend on the same few senior people. In that case, technology may simply make the organisation more efficient at doing what is becoming less relevant. These are management issues, not technology ones. They also explain why so many transformation programmes disappoint. An organisation announces a new strategy, redraws reporting lines, creates a digital team, brings in consultants and launches a new performance management system. Each of these might be sensible but none automatically changes how the organisation behaves. If people were afraid to speak honestly before the transformation they will remain afraid afterwards. If bad news is softened before reaching senior leadership a new dashboard will simply pre­­sent a cleaner version of the same reality. If managers are rewarded only for their personal results they will have little incentive to develop others. An organisation learns only when experience changes its behaviour. This requires leaders to protect the flow of difficult information. No institution can learn from a reality it is afraid to see. Leaders must distinguish respect for experience from obedience to hierarchy. Older leaders bring perspective while younger people often understand emerging technologies, customers and expectations more instinctively. Healthy organisations create a conversation between the two. The old answer to every new question is the clearest sign of institutional ageing. Pakistan’s organisations do not need to imitate every global management trend or become technology companies. They need to become learning institutions — organisations that can use technology without being defined by it, develop people without abandoning accountability, preserve purpose without protecting every old habit and change before failure makes change unavoidable. The question is not whether Pakistani organisations are ready for change and disruption. It is whether they are ready to learn. The writer advises boards and CEOs on strategy, leadership and organisational transformation. Published in Dawn, September 19th, 2026

items.title: ‘Relax, I’m not contesting you in 2028’ — DVLA CEO tells Zanetor
items.description: Chief Executive Officer of the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA), Julius Neequaye Kotey, has dismissed speculation that he is preparing to challenge Klottey Korle MP Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings in the 2028 parliamentary election. Mr Neequaye Kotey said that although he has the right to contest the constituency if he chooses to, he has not decided to do so in 2028. “If I’m eyeing that seat, it’s not against any law. I have the right to contest for that seat,” he said. He added: “For now, I have not made up my mind, so Dr Zanetor should relax. The way she is going around, she should relax. I am not going to contest her.” Mr Neequaye Kotey, popularly known as “Logas”, said his political involvement in the constituency goes back several decades. “This is my third time as a constituency executive. At age 17, I was a branch secretary for the NDC in the Korle Klottey Constituency, but I wasn’t allowed to register,” he said. He said he later served as a polling agent in 2004 before becoming a branch chairman, deputy constituency communications officer and subsequently constituency communications officer. He is currently the constituency’s Vice Chairman. Mr Neequaye Kotey also stressed his roots in the constituency, particularly Osu. “I am an indigene of Klottey Korle. I am from Osu. My hometown is Osu. I cut across all four traditional areas of Osu,” he said. The DVLA CEO said he has never concealed his political ambitions and would openly declare his intentions if he decided to contest the seat. “If I want to contest for that constituency seat, I am free. I am good and capable enough to do it, but I have said 2028; I’m not contesting,” he said. He, however, stopped short of ruling out a possible parliamentary bid beyond 2028. “I don’t know if the Lord will change my mind for subsequent years, but for 2028, I’m not contesting,” he said. He added: “Even in 2028, never say never. I can decide to contest; I don’t break any law.” “For me, I don’t hide my political ambition. If I want to contest, I will say it clearly: I want to contest,” he stated. Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings has represented Klottey Korle in Parliament since 2017. Mr Neequaye Kotey was appointed Chief Executive Officer of the DVLA in January 2025 and has since overseen reforms at the authority, including efforts to clear a backlog of driving licences and expand its services. He also recently disclosed that he had rejected an alleged GH¢4 million inducement linked to opposition to the DVLA’s new number plate reforms and said the matter had been reported to the Office of the Special Prosecutor. He spoke on Starr FM, For now, however, Mr Neequaye Kotey says he is not preparing for a parliamentary contest against Dr Agyeman-Rawlings in 2028, while leaving his political options beyond that election open.

items.title: Kloto : Des acteurs locaux sensibilisés sur les valeurs de civisme, paix et patriotisme
items.description: Kpalimé, 18 sept. (ATOP) – Des jeunes, femmes et hommes de la commune Kloto 1 ont été sensibilisés, le vendredi 18 septembre à Kpalimé, sur les valeurs citoyennes dans le cadre de la campagne « Ensemble pour le civisme, la paix et le patriotisme au Togo ». La sensibilisation est initiée par le Centre de recherches et de géopolitique internationale Firmin Têko-Agbo (CRGI-FTA), en partenariat avec la commune Kloto 1. Elle vise à renforcer la cohésion sociale, le vivre-ensemble et l’engagement des citoyens dans le développement de leur collectivité. La sensibilisation a porté sur le respect des valeurs de la République et des lois, la discipline, la tolérance, le pardon, la prévention de la violence et le patriotisme. Les participants ont également été invités à réfléchir à leur contribution au développement de leur commune à travers l’accomplissement de leurs devoirs civiques et leur participation aux initiatives d’intérêt collectif. Le responsable du CRGI-FTA, Firmin Têko-Agbo, a expliqué que cette campagne, menée depuis plus de cinq ans, repose sur la conviction que le développement d’une nation passe également par l’appropriation et la pratique des valeurs civiques et patriotiques . Il a appelé les participants, particulièrement les jeunes, à respecter les institutions et les lois de la République et à promouvoir la paix au sein des familles et des communautés. Il les a également exhortés à privilégier la tolérance et le pardon et à éviter les comportements susceptibles de favoriser la violence. M. Têko-Agbo a encouragé les citoyens à s’acquitter de leurs taxes et à prendre part aux actions de développement initiées au niveau local. La campagne du CRGI-FTA cible notamment les communes, les établissements scolaires et les universités. Elle a pour objectif de renforcer la cohésion sociale et la participation citoyenne au développement des collectivités. ATOP/ER/AYH/AO

items.title: Senate panel calls for accountability in allocation of state advertising
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Senate Stan­ding Committee on Information and Broadcasting on Friday called for stricter accountability in the allocation of state advertising. Chairman of the Committee Senator Sarmad Ali suggested that government advertisements for media organisations not registered with the EOBI should be stopped. The committee decided to seek an in-depth briefing from EOBI on the matter in its upcoming meeting. During discussion on the state of the media sector, Chairman of Committee Senator Sarmad Ali stressed the need for immediate support to strengthen the industry in the larger public interest. He said, “financial support in the shape of advertising should be provided to the mainstream media industry to combat fake news”. The committee members noted the National Press Trust purpose ceased to exist after the privatisation of its newspapers. Chairman of the committee while questioning the continuation of the Trust in its present form, remarked that the purpose of the Trust needs to be revisited. He directed that details regarding the National Press Trust’s property and funds should be presented in the next meeting. Suggestion made to stop govt advertisements for media organisations not registered with EOBI The committee decided to seek views of the law ministry on amending the NPT deed in line with changed ground realities and for the welfare of the media workers. It also decided to visit Karachi to ins­pect buildings of the NPT, PTV and Radio Pakistan to review plans for their effective utilisation. On the issue of welfare of media workers, the committee was informed that health insurance for journalists and media workers has been revived, while provision of life insurance is also being considered. The committee considered the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2025, introduced by Senator Muhammad Abdul Qadir in the Senate sitting held on Dec 1, 2025. The proposed legislation seeks to amend the composition of the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation Board by providing representation to parliamentarians, including one member from the Senate to be nominated by the Chairman of Senate and one member from the National Assembly to be nominated by the Speaker of the National Assembly. After detailed discussion, the Committee voted on the bill and apart from Senator Pervaiz Rashid all other members present voted in favour of the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2025, and accordingly it was passed by the committee. Published in Dawn, September 19th, 2026

items.title: Discipline can turn Ghana around overnight — Republic Bank MD
items.description: Republic Bank (Ghana) PLC Managing Director, Dr Benjamin Dzoboku, believes Ghana’s development challenge is less about a lack of resources and more about the discipline with which those resources are managed and utilised. According to him, a society governed by discipline, order and responsibility could achieve dramatic transformation in a relatively short period. Dr Dzoboku made the observation in an interview on Joy FM’s Personality Profile programme with Lexis Bill on Thursday, September 17, 2026, where he reflected on lessons he learnt from his childhood days as a cattle herder and how those experiences continue to shape his leadership philosophy. Dr Benjamin Dzoboku and Lexis Bill “The problem that we have in this country is not that we don’t have resources but that we don’t have discipline in society,” he said. “That is the main problem we have in this country. Is not anything. If the people are disciplined, this country can be turned overnight.” The development argument Dr Dzoboku’s comments place discipline at the centre of his broader thinking about national development. His argument is that Ghana’s ability to transform itself depends not only on what the country possesses but also on how individuals, institutions and society at large conduct themselves. He pointed to fraud as one of the consequences of a failure to maintain discipline and accountability. “But you leave them; you see what happens, they will defraud you,” he said. His observation also reflects the importance he places on order in institutional management, particularly in a financial sector where controls, accountability and responsible conduct are critical to protecting customers and maintaining confidence. Lessons from the bush Dr Dzoboku grew up in a farming family and spent part of his early life herding cattle. The experience exposed him to the behaviour of animals and the importance of understanding patterns, leadership and discipline. Years later, after rising through banking and finance to become Managing Director of Republic Bank (Ghana) PLC, those childhood observations have remained part of the principles he says influence his approach to leadership. His cattle experience has particularly reinforced his belief in observation and order. For him, leadership requires the ability to understand what is happening, establish order and ensure that people operate within clearly defined responsibilities. His reflection on cattle therefore goes beyond nostalgia about childhood. It offers an insight into the management philosophy of a banker who believes that discipline is fundamental to the success of institutions—and, ultimately, to the development of Ghana. For Dr Dzoboku, the behaviour of cattle offers a striking lesson in order and discipline. He recalled how cattle could be taken into the bush and left to themselves without necessarily wandering away, noting that they would feed within the area, rest and remain there until their handlers returned. “You can even take the cows to the bush and leave them there. They won’t go anywhere. They will eat around, and then they will sleep. You can go and come and meet them, and you come, and they will be there,” he said. That experience, he explained, often makes him compare the orderly behaviour of cattle with the conduct of people. “And you look at the way human beings behave. You ask yourself, ‘What is happening here?’” he said. Discipline at the bank The lesson has also found expression in the way he runs Republic Bank, he said, describing himself as calm but firm on discipline. “If you talk to my staff, I’m very disciplined. No, no, no. I will not allow you. I’m very calm but very disciplined,” Dr Dzoboku said. For him, discipline is not simply about enforcing rules. It is a leadership principle that provides the structure institutions and societies need to function effectively. He argued that without discipline, even abundant resources could fail to translate into meaningful development.

items.title: Législatives 2026 : Benabdallah appelle au "vote sanction"
items.description: À quatre jours des élections législatives du 23 septembre, le secrétaire général du Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS), Mohammed Nabil Benabdallah, appelle les électeurs à sortir de l’abstention et à transformer leur mécontentement en « vote sanction ». Invité vendredi soir de l’émission de Hespress « La voie vers les élections 2026 », il a également évoqué une ambition pouvant aller jusqu’à une cinquantaine de sièges, tout en posant ses conditions à une éventuelle participation au prochain gouvernement. « Votez, votez, votez, puis votez », a lancé Mohammed Nabil Benabdallah à l’adresse des électeurs. Pour le secrétaire général du PPS, l’abstention ne ferait que laisser les citoyens dans la colère sans modifier les rapports de force politiques. Le « vote sanction », tel qu’il le conçoit, doit au contraire permettre de traduire dans les urnes le mécontentement exprimé lors de la campagne. Dans les différentes étapes de son intervention, Benabdallah a décrit une colère qu’il dit avoir constatée sur le terrain à l’égard du bilan du gouvernement, évoquant notamment le coût de la vie, le chômage, la santé, l’éducation, la corruption et le clientélisme. Il a toutefois insisté sur une distinction : cette colère ne doit pas conduire au rejet indistinct de toute la classe politique ni à l’abstention. « Notre ambition, c’est le pays » Sur les perspectives électorales du PPS, le dirigeant socialiste s’est montré prudent avant de livrer une estimation. Il a d’abord rejeté l’idée que les résultats seraient déjà connus ou qu’un futur chef de gouvernement serait prédéterminé. « Notre ambition, ce n’est pas le gouvernement. Notre ambition, c’est le pays », a-t-il expliqué, affirmant que son parti entend servir le pays depuis « le site » où les électeurs lui permettront de le faire. Il a néanmoins avancé un ordre de grandeur : si le vote sanction se confirme et si une partie des électeurs abstentionnistes retourne aux urnes, le PPS pourrait figurer parmi les formations arrivant en tête. Dans une configuration où la participation et le vote sanction seraient plus limités, il estime que son parti pourrait « approcher les 50 sièges ». © Mounir Mehimdate Cette projection intervient alors que le PPS entend capitaliser sur ses sept années d’opposition et sur une campagne articulée autour du slogan « Osons ensemble ». Le parti met en avant un programme élaboré pendant plusieurs mois et comportant des engagements chiffrés sur l’emploi, l’investissement, l’éducation, la santé et la lutte contre la corruption. Benabdallah a notamment défendu l’objectif de tendre vers un million d’emplois, tout en refusant, dit-il, de présenter ce chiffre comme une promesse mécanique. Il estime qu’une création de 750.000 à 800.000 emplois constituerait déjà un résultat important. Parmi les leviers avancés figurent une industrialisation davantage orientée vers la production à forte valeur ajoutée, le développement du numérique et la création d’une banque publique d’investissement destinée à soutenir les entreprises marocaines. Le PPS propose également, selon son secrétaire général, la création de 135.000 emplois supplémentaires dans les secteurs de l’éducation et de la santé. À cela s’ajoutent des mesures portant sur le préscolaire, la réduction du nombre d’élèves par classe, le soutien financier aux familles défavorisées et le renforcement de l’offre d’internats. Pas d’entrée au gouvernement « à n’importe quel prix » L’autre enseignement majeur de l’entretien concerne les alliances qui pourraient se dessiner après le scrutin. Benabdallah a clairement indiqué que le PPS ne considère pas une participation gouvernementale comme une fin en soi. Le parti, affirme-t-il, n’entrera dans une majorité que si un accord est trouvé autour d’un socle programmatique. Parmi les priorités non négociables citées figurent la lutte contre la corruption, l’école publique, l’hôpital public, la lutte contre le chômage, la généralisation effective de la couverture sanitaire et le soutien à l’entreprise marocaine. © Mounir Mehimdate « Nous n’avons pas la participation au gouvernement comme condition », a-t-il résumé, expliquant que le PPS pourrait rester dans l’opposition si les conditions programmatiques qu’il juge essentielles ne sont pas réunies. Le dirigeant du PPS s’est montré particulièrement réservé à l’égard d’une éventuelle alliance avec le Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI), au regard des critiques formulées par son parti durant les cinq années précédentes. Il a en revanche laissé ouverte la possibilité de travailler avec d’autres formations sur la base de convergences programmatiques, citant notamment le Parti de l’Istiqlal comme exemple de formation avec laquelle des points de rencontre pourraient être identifiés. « Nous ne nous allions pas avec des personnes », a-t-il insisté. « Nous nous allions avec des projets de société » et des programmes politiques. Une manière pour le responsable du PPS de placer la question des coalitions après celle des contenus et des engagements. Du « vote sanction » à l’exercice du pouvoir Dans son dernier message, Benabdallah a finalement relié le vote sanction à une autre ambition : permettre au PPS d’exercer réellement le pouvoir. « Donnez-nous cette possibilité », a-t-il lancé, en substance, aux électeurs, estimant que le parti n’a pas encore eu l’occasion, parmi les grandes formations, de diriger effectivement le gouvernement. Il affirme que le PPS entend démontrer, dans ce cas, sa capacité à mettre en œuvre les engagements défendus pendant la campagne. Le secrétaire général rappelle aussi l’expérience gouvernementale passée de son parti, en soulignant que le PPS a participé à plusieurs gouvernements et affirme avoir continué, y compris depuis l’Exécutif, à défendre la démocratie, les libertés, la justice sociale, la transparence et les catégories les plus vulnérables. © Mounir Mehimdate Au terme de l’entretien, le message adressé aux électeurs est donc double : participer pour éviter que le mécontentement ne se traduise par une nouvelle abstention, mais aussi utiliser le bulletin de vote pour modifier le rapport de forces. « Votez et votez pour nous », a résumé Benabdallah, avant de rattacher cet appel au slogan de campagne du PPS : « Osons ensemble ». Le parti revendique ainsi une place dans le prochain paysage politique à partir d’un principe que son secrétaire général a répété durant l’émission : la participation au gouvernement n’est pas recherchée pour elle-même. Elle doit, selon lui, découler d’un mandat électoral suffisamment fort et d’un accord sur les grandes orientations à mettre en œuvre. items.title: Trump claims deal gives US control over security in Greenland
items.description: US President Donald Trump said Friday that the United States has reached an agreement with Denmark and Greenland, giving the United States "permanent control" over security and other needs in Greenland. "At my direction, we worked with representatives of Denmark and Greenland to guarantee that the United States will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. "We will immediately begin the process of developing a large Military presence in the appropriate part of Greenland, of which there are many," he said. The US president described the deal as an "Infinite Life" agreement with no expiration date and said it would come at no cost to the United States. The full text of the agreement was not immediately released. The office of Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said that the agreement is expected to be signed during the upcoming UN General Assembly and requires necessary national parliamentary procedures. Greenland is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark. Trump's earlier statements about acquiring the territory met with strong opposition from Denmark, Greenland and several European countries.

items.title: Session extraordinaire de l’AGRASC : plusieurs dossiers examinés par le CA
items.description: La session extraordinaire du Conseil d’administration de l’Agence de gestion et de recouvrement des avoirs saisis et confisqués (AGRASC) s’est tenue ce vendredi 18 septembre 2026, à Conakry. Il était question d’examiner plusieurs dossiers liés à la gestion des avoirs saisis et confisqués placés sous la responsabilité de l’Agence. Cette rencontre a également permis aux membres du Conseil d’administration de se pencher sur les mesures à envisager pour assurer leur gestion dans le respect du cadre légal et des décisions rendues par les juridictions compétentes. Les différentes options envisageables pour ces avoirs, en tenant compte de leur nature, de leur situation juridique et des dispositions applicables en matière de gestion des biens saisis et confisqués, ont été passées au peigne fin par les cadres. Une gestion axée sur la préservation des avoirs À travers cet examen, l’AGRASC entend poursuivre ses efforts en faveur d’une gestion rigoureuse et efficace des biens qui lui sont confiés. L’Agence de gestion et de recouvrement des avoirs saisis et confisqués (AGRASC), dirigée par Mohamed Diawara, veille notamment à la conservation des avoirs saisis, à la préservation de leur valeur économique et à leur administration conformément aux décisions judiciaires et aux textes qui encadrent ses missions. Pour lui et ses collaborateurs, cette Agence constitue un volet important du dispositif national de lutte contre la criminalité économique et financière. Elle nécessite, à ce titre, une approche fondée sur la rigueur, la traçabilité et le respect des procédures prévues par la législation. Les membres du Conseil d’administration ont également examiné plusieurs questions liées au fonctionnement de l’Agence et à la poursuite de ses activités, dans le cadre du renforcement de son dispositif de gestion des avoirs placés sous sa responsabilité. Après plusieurs heures d’échanges et l’examen des différents dossiers inscrits à l’ordre du jour, les travaux de la session extraordinaire se sont achevés dans la convivialité. Cette session témoigne de la volonté de l’AGRASC de consolider sa gouvernance et d’améliorer davantage les mécanismes de gestion des avoirs saisis et confisqués en République de Guinée. Elle participe également aux efforts visant à renforcer l’efficacité du dispositif national de recouvrement et de gestion des biens issus des procédures judiciaires. items.title: Bobo Dioulasso: Fermeture de l’unité de la chambre mortuaire de l’hôpital Sourô Sanou
items.description: À compter du lundi 21 septembre 2026, l'unité de la chambre mortuaire du Centre hospitalier universitaire Sourô Sanou (CHUSS) de Bobo-Dioulasso fermera temporairement ses portes jusqu'à nouvel ordre. Annoncée dans une note de service signée le 17 septembre 2026 par le Directeur général de l'établissement, Dramane Zina, cette suspension totale des activités s'inscrit dans le cadre des travaux de réhabilitation et d'extension des infrastructures hospitalières. Alors qu'un service minimum était jusqu'ici maintenu, l'engagement des travaux de gros œuvre rend désormais impossible la poursuite des prestations. Une nouvelle étape est franchie dans le projet de réhabilitation et d'extension du Centre hospitalier universitaire Sourô Sanou (CHUSS) de Bobo-Dioulasso. Par une note de service officielle diffusée le 17 septembre 2026, la Direction générale de l'hôpital a porté à la connaissance du personnel et des usagers la fermeture temporaire de l'unité de la chambre mortuaire. Cette mesure d'organisation interne fait suite aux directives arrêtées le 20 août 2026 par la Camarade Gouverneur de la région du Guiriko (communiqué N° 2026/00011/MATM/RGRK/GBD/SG), prévoyant la rénovation de plusieurs services cliniques et médico-techniques. Jusqu'à présent, l'unité mortuaire était parvenue à maintenir un service minimum malgré le démarrage du chantier. Toutefois, l'évolution des travaux et le lancement des phases de gros œuvres nécessitent aujourd'hui la libération totale des lieux afin de permettre le bon déroulement des opérations dans les conditions techniques requises. L'interruption des prestations prendra effet dès le lundi 21 septembre 2026 et se poursuivra jusqu'à nouvel ordre. Durant cette période de fermeture, aucune des prestations habituellement dispensées par la morgue ne pourra être assurée au sein du CHUSS. Le Directeur général, Dramane Zina, a invité le personnel à assurer une large diffusion de l'information et a demandé aux usagers de se conformer aux dispositifs de continuité des soins prévus dans la région. Les modalités et la date de reprise des activités feront l'objet d'une communication ultérieure dès que l'avancement des travaux le permettra. items.title: ONP : baisse de 13% des débarquements de pêche au port d'Al Hoceima
items.description: L’Office national des pêches (ONP), a fait état d’une baisse de 13% des débarquements des produits de la pêche côtière et artisanale au port d'Al Hoceima à fin août 2026, pour s’établir à 1.526 tonnes, contre 1.699 tonnes. Dans son dernier rapport sur les statistiques de la pêche côtière et artisanale au Maroc, l’ONP précise que la valeur marchande de ces captures a également reculé de 15% pour s'établir à plus de 84,67 millions de dirhams (MDH), contre environ 99,85 MDH à fin août 2025. Par espèce, les quantités de poissons pélagiques débarquées dans ce port ont régressé de 25% à 206 T, pour une valeur estimée à 8,91 MDH (-19%), contre plus de 10,99 MDH/274 T à fin août 2025. Les débarquements des poissons blancs ont augmenté de 8% à 239 T à fin août dernier, pour une valeur de plus de 10,17 MDH, contre 8,68 MDH à fin août 2025, soit une hausse de 17% en glissement annuel. Concernant les débarquement des céphalopodes, ils ont baissé de 16% atteignant 1.007 T pour des recettes d'environ 60,27 MDH (-20%), tandis que pour les crustacés, les débarquements ont évolué de 44% à 73 T, générant des revenus de plus de 5,31 MDH (+14%). Au niveau national, les débarquements des produits commercialisés de la pêche côtière et artisanale se sont établis à 723.490 T à fin août dernier, en hausse de 6% par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente. En valeur, ces débarquements ont augmenté de 1% à plus de 7,43 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) contre environ 7,37 MMDH en glissement annuel. The post ONP : baisse de 13% des débarquements de pêche au port d'Al Hoceima appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: From cowboy to Republic Bank MD – Dr. Benjamin Dzoboku tells it all
items.description: Long before he occupied the corner office of Republic Bank (Ghana) PLC, Dr Benjamin Dzoboku spent his childhood days in the cattle fields, leading herds and learning lessons in discipline, observation and leadership that he says continue to influence him to this day. The Managing Director of Republic Bank says his unlikely journey from a village near Battor in the Volta Region to the top echelons of Ghana’s banking industry began with a life that was far removed from banking. “I started as a cowboy,” Dr Dzoboku told Lexis Bill on Joy FM’s Personality Profile on Thursday, September 17, 2026. “Yeah. I was a cowboy. Even after I finished middle school, I was still leading the cows.” Born to a farming family, Dr Dzoboku said his father, who was from Mafikumikpo, a small village near Battor, was a farmer who also kept cattle, while his mother was from Battor in the North Tongu area. For several years, cattle herding was his daily routine. He would take the animals into the bush, sometimes leaving home around 5 a.m. during the dry season and returning as late as 6 or 7 p.m. “It’s a whole day of walking,” he recalled, describing a childhood that involved carrying water and food and spending long hours observing the animals. But beyond the physical demands of the work, Dr Dzoboku said the experience exposed him to a fascinating system of order and leadership among the cattle. Lessons from the herd According to him, one of the earliest lessons he learnt from the cattle was that leadership and order existed even within the animal kingdom. “You see, so as a cowboy, even though the cows are like that, they also have leaders,” he said. “Immediately you open them, the leader will take the lead.” He said the cowboy’s responsibility was often to observe the herd, understand its behaviour and direct it towards the desired destination. The animals, he explained, also responded to individual names and recognised the calls of those who tended them. “If you are a cow head or a cowboy, they know you. They also know you by language,” he said. He recalled that every cow in the herd had a name and would respond when called. The experience, he said, taught him to pay close attention to behaviour, listen carefully and understand what was happening around him before taking action. “I use my eyes a lot,” he said. “To look at things, observe.” Dr Benjamin Dzoboku and Lexis Bill That habit of observation, he suggested, remains part of his leadership style. “I observe. When I come to a place, I observe. I don’t like talking too much,” he said. Discipline as a leadership principle For Dr Dzoboku, perhaps the most important lesson from his years as a cowboy was discipline. He said cattle could be left in the bush and still remain within an established order, returning to familiar surroundings rather than wandering aimlessly. Reflecting on that experience, he said discipline had become an important principle in his management philosophy. “If you talk to my staff, I’m very disciplined,” he said. “No, no, no. I will not allow you. I’m very calm but very disciplined.” He went further to identify discipline as a major challenge facing Ghanaian society. “The problem that we have in this country is not that we don’t have resources but is discipline in society,” he said. “That is the main problem we have in this country. Is not anything. If the people are disciplined, this country can be turned overnight.” His comments underline how strongly he connects his childhood experience with his approach to leadership in the corporate world. For him, the cattle fields were not merely a place where he worked as a young boy; they were an informal classroom where he learnt to observe, listen, exercise patience and maintain order. A bicycle changed his path Interestingly, Dr Dzoboku said he did not initially dream of becoming a banker or even pursuing a professional career. After completing middle school, his father wanted him to become a transport operator and was prepared to buy him a van. “I was so much happy,” he recalled. But while he was still in the field with the cattle, his brother brought news that a secondary school was being established and encouraged him to continue his education. His first reaction was resistance. “I said, ‘No, no, no, no. Me, I want to be a transport driver.’” The deciding factor, however, was a brand-new bicycle. His family agreed to buy him one so that he could ride to school and return home. The following day, his brother bought the bicycle, and Dr Dzoboku obtained the school forms and began his secondary education. That decision would ultimately alter the course of his life. At school, he developed an interest in accounting after being inspired by his accounting teacher. “The way he was teaching accounting, I loved it,” he recalled. “I developed that interest, so from the word go I wanted to be a chartered accountant.” He also distinguished himself academically, saying he regularly placed between first and fourth position in his class. From accountant to bank chief His professional journey began with Panick and Foster before he moved to SG-SSB, later joining HFC. It was at HFC that his career began to take a decisive turn. While working in audit, he said he detected a fraud during an assignment. That caught the attention of the then Managing Director of HFC, who decided that Dr Dzoboku’s abilities could be better deployed in risk management. “I went and started as the risk manager. So I was the first person as a risk manager in HFC. I developed the first manual for HFC,” he said. He subsequently moved through several senior positions, including internal audit, finance, financial controller, treasury and retail and commercial banking. He later became General Manager of Finance and Strategy after Republic Bank of Trinidad and Tobago acquired HFC. That transition marked another significant stage in his career. He was subsequently invited to Trinidad and Tobago for what he understood was an opportunity for the group’s leadership to assess his readiness for a higher position. Initially, he resisted the move. “I didn’t want to go,” he said. He eventually accepted after his boss, Farid Antar, persuaded him to make the trip. His arrival in Trinidad coincided with the COVID-19 lockdown, which meant he spent about eight months there under unusual circumstances. Although the lockdown restricted his movement, Dr Dzoboku said the period became an important personal and professional experience. He returned to Ghana and introduced several changes within the bank before becoming Chief Operating Officer and eventually rising to the position of Managing Director. ‘I still love farming’ Despite reaching the highest level of corporate leadership, Dr Dzoboku said he has not abandoned the world from which he came. He still farms and keeps cattle. “I love that business,” he said. For someone who spent his formative years leading cattle through the bush, the continued connection to farming appears to provide a link to his beginnings. His story, however, is also one of an unexpected transformation from a young boy whose ambition was to drive a transport vehicle to a student who discovered accounting, a professional who built a career across audit, risk, finance, treasury and banking, and ultimately the Managing Director of one of Ghana’s major banks. Yet, Dr Dzoboku says some of the most enduring lessons that have shaped his leadership did not come from a business school or a boardroom. They came from the cattle fields. “Animals like cows, they hear, they listen, they are disciplined,” he said. “So if even animals can do that, then why will human beings not understand and listen?” For the Republic Bank MD, the journey from cowboy to banker has therefore been more than a remarkable career progression. It has been a journey in which the lessons of his childhood have travelled with him from the cattle fields to the corporate boardroom. items.title: Insurance sector offers huge job opportunities as Ghana faces actuarial skills shortage — GIU Rector
items.description: The insurance industry offers significant employment opportunities for young people, particularly in specialised fields such as actuarial science and statistics, Rector of the Ghana Insurance University College (GIU), Dr Richard Okyere, has said. He urged WASSCE graduates and other young people with strong interests in mathematics, data and analytical work to consider careers in insurance, saying the sector continues to face a shortage of skilled professionals. Dr Okyere said Ghana’s low insurance penetration also presented considerable room for growth, creating opportunities for professionals who can help expand the industry and manage increasingly complex financial risks. “Low insurance penetration implies huge opportunity to grow with high demand for manpower,” he said. He made the comments while speaking about the admission process and programmes offered by GIU, which was inaugurated earlier this year as a higher education institution focused on developing professionals for Ghana’s insurance and financial sectors. Dr Okyere said GIU has a distinctive advantage because it is owned by players in the insurance industry, allowing it to maintain a direct link between professional practice and academic training. “Here, the uniqueness is that there is a bridge between the industry and academia,” he said. The institution evolved from the Ghana Insurance College, established in 2006 by key industry stakeholders, including the National Insurance Commission, Ghana Insurers Association, Insurance Brokers Association of Ghana and the Chartered Insurance Institute of Ghana. Dr Okyere said the university had expanded beyond traditional professional insurance training to offer degree programmes in specialised areas. These include a Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Science with Insurance and Statistics with Insurance. “These are two specialised areas — actuarial insurance and statistics insurance. We have merged the two areas to produce professionals with both a computational mindset and an underwriting mindset,” he said. According to Dr Okyere, the programmes are intended to address a shortage of actuarial and other technical professionals in Ghana and across Africa. He said a stronger pool of local expertise was needed to help insurance companies price products appropriately, assess financial risks and make better-informed decisions. “The aim is manpower development and the technical expertise to help manage financial risks in our markets,” he said. He noted that the shortage of local expertise sometimes meant insurance and financial institutions had to rely on professionals from countries including the United Kingdom, South Africa and the United States. “This does not help the country. This promotes capital flight; the country throws away significant dollars outside the country,” he said. Dr Okyere said developing local expertise could help retain foreign exchange, strengthen the insurance industry and improve Ghana’s ability to compete in the global financial market. The Rector said GIU was also incorporating emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, financial modelling, predictive modelling and data analytics into its programmes. He said the approach was intended to prepare students for changing demands in the insurance and wider financial services sectors. Graduates, he disclosed, would receive a Bachelor of Science degree jointly issued with the University of Ghana, alongside a professional diploma in insurance administered in collaboration with an overseas professional body. Dr Okyere said experienced actuaries, statisticians, insurance practitioners, chief executive officers and academics would also be involved in teaching and mentoring students. He urged parents and prospective students to consider insurance-related programmes as viable career options, stressing that the skills acquired could be applied beyond the insurance industry. “The university is owned by the market, so the advantage of getting a job is there. Students here will have added leverage,” he said. According to him, graduates could find opportunities in sectors including banking, pensions, healthcare and manufacturing, where actuarial, statistical, financial modelling and risk management skills are increasingly relevant. Dr Okyere said GIU’s broader objective was to develop the skilled workforce needed to expand insurance coverage and strengthen financial risk management in Ghana. He therefore encouraged WASSCE certificate holders with strong analytical and cognitive interests to explore the emerging career opportunities within insurance and related sectors.

items.title: Prise en charge psychologique : L’ENAM ouvre la filière psychologie appliquée pour répondre aux enjeux de la santé mentale
items.description: Le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Camarade Mathias TRAORE, a présidé, ce vendredi 18 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la cérémonie officielle de lancement de la filière « Psychologie appliquée » de l’Ecole nationale d’administration et de magistrature (#ENAM). Placée sous le patronage du Camarade Ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, représenté par le Camarade Ministre en charge de l’Enseignement de base, Jacques Sosthène DINGARA, cette cérémonie a également connu la présence de la Camarade Ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité, Pélagie KABRE/KABORE ainsi que celle du Gouverneur de la région de Kadiogo, le Camarade Abdoulaye BASSINGA. Selon le Directeur général de l’ENAM, le Camarade Jacob Yarassoula YARABATIOULA, cette nouvelle offre de formation vise à doter l’administration publique de compétences spécialisées en matière de santé mentale, d’accompagnement psychosocial, d’orientation, de remédiation, ainsi que de gestion des crises et des traumatismes. Forte de 38 stagiaires inscrits en psychologie clinique et en psychopathologie, cette première promotion bénéficiera, selon lui, d’un encadrement rigoureux afin de répondre à la vision de la Révolution progressiste et populaire (#RPP). Dans son allocution, le Camarade Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple, Mathias TRAORE, a souligné que l’ouverture de cette filière s’inscrit dans la dynamique impulsée par le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORE, Président du Faso, Chef de l’Etat, visant à adapter continuellement les compétences des serviteurs du peuple aux réalités et aux exigences du moment. Il a rappelé que l’administration repose d’abord et avant tout sur des femmes et des hommes qui prennent les décisions, qui accueillent les usagers, qui travaillent parfois sous pression, qui sont confrontés à des situations parfois complexes et qui peuvent eux-mêmes être affectés, directement ou indirectement, par les effets de la crise que connaît notre pays. « Le lancement de cette filière ne doit donc pas être perçu comme une simple ouverture de filière académique. Il doit représenter une belle opportunité pour construire une administration mieux préparée à comprendre et à accompagner les réalités humaines auxquelles l’administration est quotidiennement confrontée », a-t-il déclaré. S’adressant aux stagiaires, le Ministre les a exhortés à incarner une promotion exemplaire, porteuse d’identité, de prestige et de crédibilité pour cette filière. « Vous avez l’obligation de travailler avec davantage de sérieux, de discipline et d’exigence. Soyez une élite, non pas une élite de privilèges, mais une élite de compétence, de probité, de travail et de service. Soyez dignes de la confiance placée en vous », a t il insisté, tout en formulant le vœu que cette filière contribue à la formation de compétences de qualité, capables de mettre leur savoir au service de l’administration, de la société et, plus largement, de la Nation. Invitant l’ENAM à faire de cette filière un modèle d’excellence, le Camarade Mathias TRAORE a exprimé sa gratitude aux responsables de l’institution, aux enseignants, chercheurs, experts, partenaires et à tous les acteurs ayant contribué à la concrétisation de ce projet. Il a particulièrement salué l’investissement du Cabinet du Camarade Président du Faso dans la réussite de cette initiative. Cette nouvelle filière est ouverte aux titulaires du Baccalauréat séries C, D ou A pour l’emploi de Psychotechnicien, ainsi qu’aux titulaires d’une Licence en Psychologie pour les emplois de Psychologue, Psychologue clinicien et Psychopathologue et Psychologue du développement et de l’éducation. items.title: 4ᵉ édition de la Bourse LONAGUI : plus de 1 000 candidats en lice, 15 jeunes retenus après un tirage au sort public
items.description: Ils étaient plus de 1 000 jeunes diplômés à espérer décrocher l’une des 15 places disponibles. Après plusieurs étapes de sélection, les bénéficiaires de la quatrième édition de la « Bourse LONAGUI » ont été dévoilés ce vendredi 18 septembre à Conakry, au cours d’une cérémonie marquée par un tirage au sort public supervisé par un huissier de justice. Cette nouvelle édition a suscité un fort engouement auprès des étudiants guinéens. Des candidatures venues de Conakry, mais également des universités de l’intérieur du pays, ont été enregistrées par la Loterie Nationale de Guinée. À l’issue de l’examen des dossiers, les candidats répondant aux critères établis ont participé à un processus de sélection présenté par les organisateurs comme transparent et équitable. Les bénéficiaires retenus, tous titulaires d’une licence avec la mention Bien et âgés de moins de 35 ans, poursuivront leurs études en Master 1 et Master 2 dans des établissements d’enseignement supérieur guinéens. Leur formation sera entièrement prise en charge dans le cadre de cette initiative. Cette quatrième édition a été organisée autour de plusieurs catégories afin de prendre en compte différents profils. Sur les 15 bourses attribuées, six concernent les filières scientifiques, quatre les domaines littéraire et économique, trois sont réservées aux jeunes femmes, une relève de la catégorie « Coup de cœur » et une autre de la bourse sociale destinée aux candidats confrontés à des situations particulières. Présent à la cérémonie, Keita Ibrahima Kalil, Directeur général adjoint chargé de l’administration de la LONAGUI, a expliqué les motivations qui ont conduit à la mise en place de ce programme. Selon lui, l’initiative s’inscrit dans la responsabilité sociétale de l’entreprise. « Dès l'entame, j'avais signalé ici que la Loterie Nationale de Guinée, c'est une entité publique. C'est une entité qui fait de l'épargne publique volontaire et redistribuée aux citoyens guinéens. Donc vous n'êtes pas sans savoir que lorsqu'une entreprise se trouve dans cette démarche, elle a une vocation RSE fondamentalement », a-t-il rappelé. Poursuivant son intervention, le DGA chargé de l’administration a expliqué que la formation des jeunes constitue l’un des axes prioritaires de cette démarche. « Dans l'ensemble de nos activités RSE que nous engageons, on a vu plus judicieux, et conformément à la volonté de faire de la formation des jeunes une priorité nationale, on a mis en place cette Bourse LONAGUI pour permettre aux jeunes qui souhaitent se performer, pour donner des opportunités à ces jeunes pour continuer leur parcours académique », a-t-il indiqué. Pour accéder à cette bourse, les candidats devaient notamment être de nationalité guinéenne, avoir moins de 35 ans, être titulaires d’une licence avec la mention Bien et présenter un projet professionnel. Mais pour la LONAGUI, le processus ne s’est pas limité à un simple tirage au sort. Keita Ibrahima Kalil a expliqué que des dispositions ont été prises en amont afin de sélectionner des candidats capables de poursuivre leur parcours universitaire. « Avant de venir recruter, donner la chance aux jeunes, il y a tout un ensemble de mécanismes derrière. Nous contactons l'ensemble des filières qui sont des besoins réels de notre société, des écoles, des institutions. On discute avec eux sur les modalités de scolarité, sur les critères, sur un ensemble d'aspects qui nous permettront d'évaluer », a-t-il expliqué. Avec plus de 1 000 candidats enregistrés, un travail de présélection a donc été réalisé avant l’étape finale. « Il ne s'agit pas de donner la chance à quelqu'un, il faut donner la chance à quelqu'un qui est prêt à parcourir le cycle », a insisté le responsable. Revenant sur le déroulement du tirage, Keita Ibrahima Kalil a également expliqué les dispositions prises pour favoriser une meilleure représentativité des profils. « Vous avez vu, on a fait un premier tirage, c'est parti, il y avait moins de dames. On s'est dit pour équilibrer, il faut regrouper les dames dans un seul endroit pour pouvoir faire un autre tirage. Et en plus, on a réuni d'un autre côté ceux qui sont à leur troisième, quatrième participation, un parcours spécial. Et en plus de ça, on a réuni aussi les personnes à mobilité réduite », a-t-il précisé. Pour lui, cette organisation traduit la volonté d’offrir les mêmes possibilités aux jeunes, quels que soient leurs profils. « L'ensemble de ces critères réunis prouve à suffisance que nous voulons donner les mêmes opportunités, les mêmes chances à tous les jeunes guinéens qui souhaitent parfaire leur parcours académique », a-t-il soutenu. Le responsable de la LONAGUI a par ailleurs invité les jeunes guinéens à s’intéresser davantage à ce programme. « L'opportunité ça vient, la chance vient sous une forme d'opportunité, il faut la saisir. Quand ils verront partout la Bourse LONAGUI, de s'intéresser. Et ensuite, dans les démarches, ils se rendront compte que c'est la chance qui va leur sourire pour qu'ils se retrouvent boursiers de la Loterie Nationale », a-t-il lancé. Mme Jacqueline Coker, Conseillère chargée des actions sociales, représentant le Directeur général de la LONAGUI, a rappelé la portée sociale de cette initiative. « Le véritable bénéfice d’une nation ne se mesure pas uniquement dans ses chiffres financiers. Il se mesure à l’éclat du savoir de sa jeunesse, à l’égalité des chances que nous créons, et aux portes que nous ouvrons », a-t-elle déclaré. Elle a rappelé que depuis le lancement du programme en 2023, plus de 40 jeunes ont déjà bénéficié d’une prise en charge de leur cursus. De son côté, Mme Nene Satourou Barry, représentante du Conseil d’administration, a salué le travail effectué par la commission d’organisation. « Aucune transformation économique durable ne peut se construire sans investir dans le capital humain. La Bourse LONAGUI traduit une volonté claire : n'exclure personne et donner sa chance à chaque talent, quel que soit son parcours », a-t-elle indiqué. Pour les nouveaux boursiers, cette sélection représente une étape importante dans leur parcours. Abdoulaye Keita, diplômé en Logistique et Transport de l’Université Gamal Abdel Nasser de Conakry, s’est engagé à honorer cette confiance. « Je m'engage à donner le meilleur de moi-même dans mes études et à prouver que cette confiance est méritée. C'est une opportunité unique de réaliser mon projet professionnel », a-t-il déclaré. Fatoumata Bangoura, diplômée en Pêche et Aquaculture à l’Institut Supérieur des Sciences de Médecine Vétérinaire de Dalaba, estime également que cette bourse correspond à ses ambitions. « Cette bourse correspond parfaitement à mes objectifs. Je m'engage avec sérieux à me former pour revenir servir ma nation », a-t-elle affirmé. Avec cette quatrième édition, la LONAGUI offre à ces 15 nouveaux bénéficiaires ,un nouveau chapitre de leur parcours académique, avec l’objectif de transformer cette opportunité en réussite. Christine Finda Kamano L’article 4ᵉ édition de la Bourse LONAGUI : plus de 1 000 candidats en lice, 15 jeunes retenus après un tirage au sort public est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Affaire Lionel Bilgo : Le blanchiment de capitaux conduit le TGI de Bobo-Dioulasso à se dessaisir au profit du pôle ECOFI
items.description: Le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Bobo-Dioulasso s'est dessaisi, ce vendredi 18 septembre 2026, du dossier impliquant l'ancien ministre Wendkouni Joël Lionel Bilgo et son collaborateur Vincent de Paul Kaboré, directeur exécutif de la Société immobilière Traoré et frères (SITRAF), au profit du pôle économique et financier (ECOFI). La décision intervient à la suite des enquêtes complémentaires qui ont notamment fait apparaître une nouvelle qualification de blanchiment de capitaux, en plus des infractions initialement reprochées aux deux prévenus. À l'ouverture de l'audience, le ministère public a demandé au président du TGI de se dessaisir du dossier au profit du pôle ECOFI. Le parquet a expliqué que les investigations complémentaires ordonnées lors du premier renvoi de l'affaire avaient permis de mettre en évidence de nouveaux éléments, notamment concernant des faits susceptibles de relever du blanchiment de capitaux. Pour le ministère public, cette nouvelle donne justifie que le dossier soit désormais examiné par le pôle ECOFI, compétent pour connaître des infractions économiques et financières. Le parquet a ainsi estimé que le dessaisissement du TGI au profit de cette juridiction spécialisée répondait à un souci de « bonne administration de la justice ». La défense de Lionel Bilgo et de Vincent de Paul Kaboré a contesté cette demande. Les avocats ont estimé qu'il n'existait pas de fondement juridique suffisant pour justifier le dessaisissement du TGI. Selon eux, les infractions initialement poursuivies relèvent de la compétence du Tribunal de grande instance. Ils ont donc demandé que l'affaire soit retenue et jugée au fond par la juridiction saisie. Mais pour le ministère public, les résultats des investigations supplémentaires ont changé la nature du dossier. En plus de l'« exercice illégal d'activités de promotion foncière » et de la « publicité d'activités de promotion immobilière sans autorisation préalable », l'enquête a fait ressortir le blanchiment de capitaux. C'est notamment cette nouvelle qualification qui a conforté la demande de transfert du dossier vers le pôle ECOFI. Après avoir entendu les différentes parties, le président du Tribunal a suspendu l'audience afin de délibérer. À la reprise, le Tribunal a finalement ordonné le dessaisissement du TGI de Bobo-Dioulasso au profit du pôle ECOFI, au nom de la « bonne administration de la justice ». Le dossier devra donc désormais poursuivre son cours devant cette juridiction spécialisée, où les faits nouvellement révélés par l'enquête complémentaire pourront être examinés dans le cadre de la procédure. Le Tribunal a également décidé du maintien en détention des deux prévenus. Lionel Bilgo et Vincent de Paul Kaboré restent ainsi détenus dans l'attente de la suite de la procédure devant le pôle ECOFI. Pour rappel, les deux hommes avaient comparu pour la première fois le 4 septembre 2026 devant le TGI de Bobo-Dioulasso. Ils étaient alors poursuivis pour « exercice illégal d'activités de promotion foncière » et « publicité d'activités de promotion immobilière sans autorisation préalable ». Le parquet avait obtenu le renvoi du dossier au 18 septembre afin de procéder à des actes de poursuite complémentaires. La défense avait sollicité la liberté provisoire pour les prévenus, mais le Tribunal avait rejeté cette demande et maintenu les deux hommes en détention. Romuald Dofini Lefaso.net

items.title: Newsfile to discuss Ghana Jollof nurse case, cocaine shipment, COVID audit and constitutional reforms
items.description: JoyNews’ flagship current affairs programme, Newsfile , will on Saturday, September 19, 2026, examine four major national issues that have dominated public discourse over the past week. Hosted by Samson Lardy Anyenini, the programme will air from 8:00am to 12:00pm on Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews and other platforms. Ghana Jollof case and the free speech debate The programme will examine the arrest and remand of 40-year-old senior nursing officer Salomey Awiti Bafoh over her alleged links to the controversial “Ghana Jollof” TikTok account. Ms Bafoh was arrested at her home in Hansua, near Techiman, on September 13 and later appeared before the Adentan Circuit Court, where she pleaded not guilty to a charge of abetment of crime, specifically the alleged publication and circulation of false news under Sections 20(1) and 208 of the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29). She was denied bail and remanded for two weeks, with the case adjourned to September 30. The prosecution alleges that Ms Bafoh acted as a liaison for UK-based TikTok user Barbara Asantewaa Kodua, popularly known as “Ghana Jollof”, and helped recruit others to redistribute videos produced by Kodua. The allegations, including claims that some of the videos contained inflammatory statements capable of provoking violence, have not been established by the court. The case has triggered a wider debate about freedom of expression and the use of state security agencies. NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has called for Ms Bafoh’s release, describing the circumstances surrounding her arrest and detention as “very worrying” and warning against infringements on free speech. Newsfile will examine the legal, constitutional and broader democratic questions arising from the case. 3.9-tonne cocaine shipment and Ghana’s security systems The programme will also turn to the seizure of nearly 3.9 tonnes of suspected cocaine by French customs at the Port of Dunkirk on September 10. The consignment, concealed in a container carrying plastic waste that had departed from Ghana, was valued at about €225 million. Six people have since been denied bail by the Kwabenya Circuit Court in connection with the shipment. Four of those accused are linked to the Ghana Revenue Authority and face allegations relating to the handling of Customs scanning procedures at Tema Port. President John Dramani Mahama has subsequently directed the formation of an inter-agency task force to develop a roadmap for strengthening measures to prevent drug trafficking through Ghana’s borders. The task force has been given two weeks to submit its recommendations, while 10 people, including four Customs officers, are currently being held as investigations continue. The programme will examine questions surrounding the shipment, Ghana’s port and border security systems, and the wider implications of the seizure. COVID-19 fumigation expenditure under scrutiny Newsfile will further examine questions surrounding COVID-19 fumigation expenditure and the apparent disparity between the Auditor-General’s special audit and figures uncovered by investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni. The Auditor-General’s special audit reported GH¢96.3 million in COVID-19 fumigation expenditure. However, documents from the Ministries of Education, Local Government and Transport cited in Mr Awuni’s investigation point to at least GH¢780 million spent on fumigation between 2020 and 2022. The investigation found that Zoomlion Ghana Limited received about GH¢775 million of the amount identified. The discrepancy has prompted questions about what was captured in the special audit and why some expenditure identified in the various ministries was not reflected in the reported figure. Vice Chairperson of Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee, Davis Ansah Opoku, has said there is no basis for arrests at this stage, arguing that the immediate priority should be for the Audit Service to explain why expenditure by the Ministries of Local Government and Transport was not captured. The programme will explore the figures, the audit process and the accountability questions arising from the findings. Constitutional review and calls for broader consensus The fourth issue will be the growing debate over Ghana’s ongoing constitutional review process. The New Patriotic Party has rejected the proposed extension of the presidential and parliamentary terms from four to five years and has called for a Constituent or Consultative Assembly to deliberate on the proposed reforms. The party has also criticised the scale and process of the proposed amendments, arguing that changes affecting a substantial portion of the 1992 Constitution require broader deliberation. The concerns extend beyond the NPP. More than 100 civil society organisations, labour groups and professional bodies under the Citizens’ Platform on Constitutional Reform have called for the process to be backed by legislation and clear timelines, while urging greater citizen participation. The Citizens’ Platform has also rejected the proposed five-year presidential term, arguing that the current four-year mandate can be retained alongside other reforms to improve governance and accountability. The government, however, has rejected the NPP’s demand for a Consultative Assembly, describing the proposal as without merit and pointing to the fact that the review process has been underway for almost two years. Newsfile will examine the competing positions, the proposed changes and the broader question of how Ghana should reach consensus on reforms to its constitutional order. The four issues will form the focus of Saturday’s edition as Newsfile brings together its host and panellists to interrogate developments shaping the national conversation.

items.title: Siliana | Un enfant de 8 ans meurt emporté par les eaux d’un oued en crue
items.description: Les unités de la Protection civile de Siliana ont repêché, ce vendredi soir, le corps sans vie d'un enfant âgé de 8 ans, emporté par les eaux en crue de l'oued à Rouhia. Originaire de la délégation de Sbeïtla, la jeune victime était en visite chez des proches dans la région depuis quelques jours, a indiqué un responsable local à l'agence Tap. Selon la même source, le drame s'est produit alors que l'enfant accompagnait son cousin de 12 ans. En tentant de traverser l'oued pour regagner leur domicile, les deux enfants ont été balayés par la force du courant. Si le plus jeune a tragiquement perdu la vie, le second a pu être secouru avant d'être évacué vers l'hôpital local de Rouhia, où son état de santé est jugé stable par les équipes médicales. Y. N. items.title: Can the Never-Trump Coalition Last?
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. George F. Will joined The Washington Post when Richard Nixon was president, and he’s been espousing the same cerebral brand of conservatism twice a week ever since. His record doesn’t leave much room for surprise. And yet, there Will was on September 16, encouraging South Carolina voters to elect not Darline Graham, the Donald Trump protégé and newly appointed Republican senator vying for a complete term, but Annie Andrews , a Democrat running on a platform that includes abortion rights, expanded health entitlements, and higher wages for workers. Around the same time, Karl Rove —who’s been deeply enmeshed in Republican politics since he was a teenager in the 1960s— announced that this fall he would vote for a Democrat for only the second time in his life rather than support Bo French, the GOP nominee for Texas railroad commissioner, following racist remarks French made about South Asian students at the University of Texas. (Rove didn’t couch his remarks as a commentary on Trump, but the president correctly understood it as pushback on Trump ism , and attacked Rove.) Each of these record-scratch moments is a distinctive product of the Trump era. The desire to resist the president continues to create some strange bedfellows, but the question is whether this alliance can survive the end of the Trump presidency—and, if not, what will become of its parts. Over the past decade, disgust with Trump has led many Republicans and conservatives to disavow him or the GOP—some over policy (for example, Trump’s critique of free trade), others over character (say, the Access Hollywood video), and still others over some combination thereof. Some who opposed Trump in 2016 made their peace once he won the election. In January 2016, National Review gathered a range of conservative writers in an “Against Trump” package. Today, many of those writers have broken for Trump, and the magazine generally supports the president. Others, however, have remained firm—those now known as “never-Trumpers.” Five years ago, my colleague David Frum quoted a common dismissal : “Never Trump is not a political party. It is a dinner party.” But, as Frum wrote, raw numbers understate never-Trumpers’ impact. The combination of disaffected Republican and independent voters and prominent anti-Trump pundits has helped establish an important political bloc. An anti-MAGA majority emerged in the 2018, 2020, and 2022 elections, improbably including both the democratic socialist Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and the quintessential neoconservative Bill Kristol. The bloc splintered in 2024 but appears to be reconstituting itself ahead of the midterm elections. The never-Trump group includes distinct factions. Although moderate Republicans are heavily represented in the exodus, some members, such as former Representative Liz Cheney, are very conservative. Some emphasize that they remain on the right. Jeff Flake, a former senator from Arizona, served as an ambassador in the Biden administration, but he recently told my colleague Adam Harris , “I’m still a registered Republican, and I’m hoping that the party returns to its previous kind of tenets of limited government, economic freedom, individual responsibility, strong American leadership abroad.” Many have registered as independents, and others have become Democrats. As that party moves left, Never-Trumpers have become the party’s de facto moderate wing. Kristol now sometimes takes positions bolder than and to the left of Democratic Party leaders’, and has embraced “Woke Bill Kristol” memes. As Trump slides toward lame-duck status, cleavages within the group and between it and traditional progressives are becoming more salient. Some stalwart anti-Trumpers and former Republicans have unsuccessfully run for office as Democrats. Geoff Duncan, a former GOP lieutenant governor of Georgia who spoke at the 2024 Democratic National Convention, lost the Democratic primary for governor this year. The lawyer and writer George Conway finished fifth in a Manhattan U.S. House primary. Frequent appearances on MS NOW can make someone a hero to progressives, but that doesn’t necessarily translate into votes. The prominence of avowedly left-wing candidates also puts pressure on the coalition. Former Republicans could make their peace with Joe Biden, but Democrats such as New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed are going to be tougher sells if you’re in favor of small government or a close alliance with Israel. Trump’s war with Iran has also created tensions, with some neocons including Kristol backing the concept of attacking Iran even as they’ve criticized the way Trump is handling it. Upheaval might be coming to political media too. Disaffected conservatives have created new publications, such as The Bulwark and The Contrarian , that cater to a spectrum of readers, from moderate Republicans to mainstream Democrats. Other defectors have prominent posts in liberal outlets: Nicolle Wallace, a former George W. Bush communications director, hosts a daily show on MS NOW, and David French is a New York Times columnist. What will become of these audiences when resisting Trump is no longer a unifying force? Some readers and viewers may stick around and even start to hear conservative ideas more sympathetically, but others who currently thrill at seeing former conservatives skewering Trump may find that they no longer have much politically in common with the pundits. Although the establishment of the broad pro-democracy bloc that set aside other disagreements was a necessary response to a political crisis, its eventual dissolution will also probably be a sign of civic health. Although they agree on democratic norms, the anti-Trump factions have valid disagreements on a range of policies, which are hard to hash out under one tent. (Consider Democratic Party leaders’ struggles to maintain unity.) In a healthy country, politics isn’t organized entirely around one person. Such a situation leaves only two options: for and against. An even better system might allow for a range of small parties that could form and dissolve many overlapping, ad hoc coalitions around specific issues of agreement, but the current U.S. electoral structure makes more than two parties all but impossible . Perhaps the end of the Trump era will clear the way for reforms that will not only restore but also improve American democracy. Related: Never Trump, still a Republican America has an anti-MAGA majority. (From 2022) Here are three new stories from The Atlantic : Jon Ossoff is doing something different. Thomas Chatterton Williams on the other way AI impairs our thinking What the Kennedy Center’s tax return reveals Today’s News The Trump administration approved a potential $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets and related equipment to Saudi Arabia , according to a statement yesterday from the State Department. The deal still requires congressional approval and would make Saudi Arabia the second country in the Middle East, after Israel, to operate the advanced stealth fighters. President Trump said in a social-media post that he is banning CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House “as ​a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” Trump also said that he would announce additional outlets to be banned. The U.S. military nearly intercepted a Chinese ship in the Middle East this spring after an AI-assisted intelligence report falsely identified its cargo as components for a nuclear-weapons program, sources familiar with the incident said. Officials discovered the error shortly before the planned operation, after military personnel had begun preparing to board the vessel. Sources: Getty City Rats Are Going on Birth Control By Emma Marris A city can have one of two levels of rat. There are cities where rats are glimpsed at night, furtively scurrying into a dark corner or among the train tracks. Then there are cities where the rats are so numerous and so brazen that they work out private disputes by brawling midday on a train platform, or they lounge on your front porch, eating fallen fruit. When rats reach that second level, city officials need some answer, any answer, to their rat problem. Washington, D.C., has reached that level, and Mayor Muriel Bowser’s answer involves rat birth control. Read the full article. More From The Atlantic Luis Parrales: When George W.
